claims: Reviewed production/test claims completed in ROUTING.md
scope: Only parent-authored schema record_count/possible_record and encode integration, plus independent new prefix/count/oracle tests. Existing harness/workflow and earlier production review retained; no self-approval of reviewer-authored workflow.
checks: The LF count is exactly min(old inclusive-record count, MAX_RECORDS+1): each LF terminates one record; only a nonempty unterminated tail adds one. Early saturation is valid before examining the remaining tail. Empty/trailing-LF cases preserve zero/no-extra-record behavior.

Before each 64KiB slice count<=MAX_RECORDS; each slice adds<=65536. With current constants the largest intermediate is131072, and the final result is<=65537. MAX_TARGET remains checked before counting; no new allocation, unsafe operation, unchecked input-derived offset or decoder change.

possible_record short-circuits oversized records before whitespace scanning and uses the exact existing space/tab/CR/LF definition. All parser-admitted templates require the opening brace in their first literal fragment. Rejecting another prefix cannot match or spend comparison budget; valid-looking but malformed/invalid-UTF8 brace inputs retain the original validation path.

The new branch runs only while work<MAX_MATCH_WORK; exhausted-budget behavior remains on the old path. Full SCVAL001 representation and unchanged prepared zstd compression remain byte-identical by the retained oracle tests.

New tests cover all256 leading bytes, non-JSON whitespace, empty/whitespace-only inputs, malformed brace prefixes, exact/oversized record lengths, 64KiB boundaries and MAX_RECORDS saturation with both terminated and unterminated tails. The existing check helper compares full ordinary/prepared SCVAL001 bytes, decodes exact target bytes and compares compressed frames against the frozen encoder.
limitations: Readiness for one separately registered phase2 local campaign, not performance acceptance or WAN permission independent of registered gates.
Phase1 700-operation failure remains separate; original thresholds/dose are unchanged and no data pooling is authorized.
Unchanged receiver authentication, durable commit, harness accounting and workflow remain covered by their prior independent reviews; no broad security/dependency audit was performed.
